messages.subject_clean: featureCounts parameters: −− fracOverlap −− fracOverlapFeature + recuwest for a parameter
messages.body_plain:
Hello
 I have problem with the parameters −− fracOverlap −− fracOverlapFeature, there is either a bug or I do not understand them properly:

I have sam file:
@HD    VN:1.0    SO:coordinate
@SQ    SN:NC_000913.2    LN:4639675
@RG    ID:N1_phred64_gap100
@PG    ID:bowtie2    PN:bowtie2    VN:2.0.0-beta7
FCC4RN3ACXX:8:1101:13114:2637#GTAGAGAT    0    NC_000913.2    104715    255    27M    *    0    0    ACGCCTTTGGCACGCCGCCAAGCGACG    FGEJIIGGJIIIJJJJJJJJIIGHGHH    AS:i:0    XN:i:0    XM:i:0    XO:i:0    XG:i:0    NM:i:0    MD:Z:27    YT:Z:CP    RG:Z:N1_phred64_gap100    NH:i:1

I have SAF file:
Geneid    Chr    Start    End    Strand    Length
FM_+NC_000913.2_104718_23    NC_000913.2    104719    104741    +

I use command:
~/subread/subread-1.6.0-Linux-x86_64/bin/featureCounts -T 1 -M -O -s 1 -F SAF -R SAM --fracOverlap 0.888 --fracOverlapFeature 0.888 -a 1.SAF -o 1_counted.SAF 1.sam

For some reason the read gets counted.
Length of the read is 27 and feature is 23. The feature overlaps fraction 23/27 = ~0.852 But the limit was set to 0.888.

Request for a parameter:
Mostly I would be interested in a feature where you could set overlap not by the fraction but number of bases which could be missing.

For example:
I would like to set that the read and the feature can be different by two bases:
in that case my read and feature woulnd not match.

Best,
Hannes

messages.subject: Re: featureCounts parameters: −− fracOverlap −− fracOverlapFeature + recuwest for a parameter
messages.subject_clean: featureCounts parameters: −− fracOverlap −− fracOverlapFeature + recuwest for a parameter
messages.body_plain:
Dear Hannes,

This is because of the round-up error when converting a float number to a integer. In other words, the algorithm works in this way:

1) calculate the effective read length (27 in your case)
2) calculate the minimum threshold to the # of overlapping bases in read (27 * 0.888 = 23.98; int(23.98) = 23)
3) compare the threshold (23) with the actual # of overlapping bases (23).

I calculated the threshold first because floating number operations are usually slow, so I only calculate it once for each read/read-pair. It would be a very little slower if I calculate the fractions of bases for each overlapping exon, and compare the fractions with the required fraction.

> set overlap not by the fraction but number of bases which could be missing

Thanks for your suggestion. It seems that this is particularly useful when the read lengths are variable, if I'm right?

Cheers,
Yang

messages.subject: featureCounts : limits on multioverlap (option -O) ?
messages.body_plain:
Hello everybody,

I'm running featureCounts (version 1.6.0) with an annotation in SAF format, this way :

> /home/marc/Downloads/subread-1.6.0-Linux-x86_64/bin/featureCounts -F SAF -L -T 3 -O -a saf.test -o /home/marc/Desktop/test_result exon.bam promoter.bam intron.bam five_prime_utr.bam three_prime_utr.bam intergenic.bam

saf.test contains for the 1st run, 50 features, all intentionally on the same region, with the same start & end (overlapping features). The reads were assigned as expected (all the 50 features have the same number of reads).

I have done this test in increasing the number of features, and I saw that for a number of 5000 overlapping features for example, no reads were assigned at all, even though on the screen, I can see it is said that the reads were assigned.

I'm doing these tests, because I want to replace an other tool by featureCounts because of its high speed, and I want to be sure it is free of unexpected results.

So, my question is the following : is there a limit in the number of handled overlapping features by the program ?

Thanks in advance !

Best,

Marc

messages.subject: Re: featureCounts : limits on multioverlap (option -O) ?
messages.body_plain:
Yes, there is a hard limit ("MAX_HIT_NUMBER") to the overlapping exons. You can find it in readSummary.c.

The value for MAX_HIT_NUMBER is 3000. You can change it to a larger number and rebuild the programs, if you want more overlapping exons being handled.

messages.subject: featureCount over counting multi-mapping long reads
messages.subject_clean: featureCount over counting multi-mapping long reads
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I came across an issue while using featureCounts to quantify long read datasets and wanted to report that. It does not seem to handle multi-mapping reads correctly, as output by the aligner, minimap2. I've attached a small sample file where one read has 7 possible alignments. I run featureCounts with the "-L", "-M", "-O", and "--fraction" flags. However, the output I get still treats it as 7 separate alignments, which should not be the case and the total count in output is given 6. I was wondering why that would happen? Note that the read is aligned against the mm10 mouse genome. I can email the output file for this as well if needed. This was just a test case, but I've encountered multiple cases where there's multi-mapping and featureCounts overcounts the total number of reads and, in turn, expressed features. Let me know if I should be using different parameters. Would be grateful for your help.

-Laraib

Command I ran: "/subread-1.5.3-Linux-x86_64/bin/featureCounts -t exon -g gene_id -a Mus_musculus.GRCm38.84.gtf -o out.txt longSingle.sam -L -O -M --fraction"

messages.subject: Re: featureCount over counting multi-mapping long reads
messages.subject_clean: featureCount over counting multi-mapping long reads
messages.body_plain:
Hi Laraib,

The alignment records in your SAM file don't have the "NH" tag. According to SAM tag specification

   https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/SAMtags.pdf

, "NH" tag is a standard tag for "number of reported alignments that contains the query in the current record". Other mainstream read aligners (inc. Subread), as we have tested, have this "NH" tag for the multi-mapping reads.

If this tag is missing, featureCounts cannot tell if a read was mapped multiple times in the input SAM/BAM file.

Cheers,
Yang
